implementation_statement: No security policy was in force at fieldwork; an MSP-supplied template was never adopted. POL-02 (access control, with program governance and supplier rules) was approved 2026-08-31 and takes effect 2026-09-01. A one-page onboarding and offboarding checklist is due 2026-09-30.

implementation_statement: The Operations Manager requests accounts; the MSP creates suite and laptop accounts; the Operations Manager creates ERP and supplier portal accounts. Gaps: no termination checklist (the former setup technician's ERP account stayed active from 2025-11 until 2026-07-15); one distributor portal login is shared by 3 staff and the carrier account by everyone; no periodic account review.

implementation_statement: ERP roles limit quoting, purchasing, accounting, and administration. Gap: the suite's Orders folder, which holds DoD equipment lists (FCI), is open to all 7 staff, including staff who never work DoD orders.
evidence: ERP role list; Orders folder permission report (2026-07-16)

implementation_statement: Staff have no local administrator rights on laptops (MSP policy). Gaps: 3 staff hold ERP administrator roles (target 2: Owner and Operations Manager); the setup bench desktop uses a shared local administrator account.
evidence: ERP role list; MSP endpoint policy

implementation_statement: The MSP enforces a 10-minute screen lock on laptops. Gap: the setup bench desktop is exempt because the technician found the lock inconvenient during imaging.

Staff reach the SaaS systems over the internet with MFA; there is no VPN. The MSP reaches all 9 computers through its RMM tool (SYS-08). Gap: no evidence that the RMM tool requires MFA for technicians or of which technicians have access.

Staff read suite email on personal phones (mail app with MFA, no device management), and two staff have received supplier files through personal email. Supplier portals (SYS-06) and banking (SYS-07) are external systems used daily. No rule limits which external systems may hold FCI.

The Owner updates the company website and online marketplace listings, which are hosted outside the boundary. A review on 2026-07-20 found no FCI posted. Gap: no written rule that DoD customer names, order photos, or delivery details are never posted, and no review before posting.

There is no security training; the MSP sends occasional phishing warnings. Planned: annual training covering FCI handling, supplier payment fraud, counterfeit and Section 889 awareness, and incident reporting, with quarterly phishing simulations from 2026-10.

The ERP logs sign-ins, user actions, and changes to supplier bank details; the suite logs sign-ins and file access at default settings. Gap: firewall events are kept only by the MSP and the events to log are not defined.
evidence: ERP audit log sample; suite audit settings

control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting
implementation_statement: Gap: nobody reviews logs. Planned: a monthly 30-minute review of ERP administrator activity and supplier bank-detail changes, suite sign-in alerts, and new mail forwarding rules, from 2026-10, recorded on a checklist.

An independent consultant assessed 14 controls on 2026-08-10 to 2026-08-12 (P07). This is not the CMMC Level 1 self-assessment; that uses the SP 800-171A objectives for the 15 FAR requirements and is planned for 2026-10-31 (P03).

The MSP's RMM tool lists the 9 computers. Gap: no inventory of network devices, cameras, scanners, SaaS services, or where FCI is stored, and none of the company's own equipment had been checked against the Section 889 covered list (P07 later found the camera recorder is covered). Planned: one-page inventory with manufacturer of record by 2026-10-31.
Gap: no contingency plan. Planned: a 2-page plan built from the BIA (P05) with work-from-home steps, distributor phone ordering, the federal reporting kit, and a hurricane checklist, by 2026-11-30.
Gap: the suite backup (SYS-05) has never been restore-tested. Planned: first restore test 2026-09-30, then quarterly; annual tabletop with the P08 runbook.

provider_if_inherited: ERP vendor; backup service (through the MSP)
implementation_statement: The ERP vendor backs up ERP data (SOC 2 report, P09). The MSP copies the suite nightly to SYS-05 with 30 days of versions. Gaps: copies are not immutable; the backup console administrator login has no MFA; customer settings files on the setup bench are not backed up.
evidence: ERP vendor SOC 2 report; SYS-05 job report (MSP)

implementation_statement: Every staff member has a unique ERP and suite account. Gaps: shared distributor portal and carrier logins; shared local administrator account on the setup bench.
evidence: ERP user list; suite user export; P07 test

implementation_statement: MFA is enforced for all ERP and suite accounts, including administrators. Gaps: the backup console (MSP-held), the firewall management login, and the distributor portal administrator account accept a password only.
evidence: ERP and suite MFA settings; P07 test 2026-08-11

implementation_statement: SaaS password rules use vendor defaults. Gaps: passwords for the shared portal and carrier accounts sit in a spreadsheet in the Orders folder; the staff Wi-Fi password has not changed since 2022.

The P08 runbook (approved 2026-08-31) makes the Owner incident lead with the Operations Manager as coordinator, the MSP for technical response, and the insurer's panel counsel and forensic firm. Gap: not yet tested; the April 2026 payment diversion was handled ad hoc and not reported.
evidence: P08 runbook; MSP contract; insurance policy

implementation_statement: POL-03 requires staff to report suspected incidents and suspect products to the Operations Manager within 1 hour, and sets the 1-business-day Section 889 report. Gaps: staff have not yet been told (training due 2026-10-31), and nobody has a DIBNet account.
The P08 supplier compromise runbook, with its contact list and notification matrix, serves as the incident response plan at this tier.
The MSP wipes laptops before reuse when asked. Gaps: two laptops retired in 2025 went to an e-waste drop-off with no wipe record; no procedure for setup bench drives.

Office and stockroom doors are keyed, with an intrusion alarm; keys are held by the Owner, the Operations Manager, and the technician. Gaps: the stockroom door is propped open during deliveries; the alarm code is shared by all staff and has never changed; no key log.
Gap: no visitor log; couriers and customers enter the stockroom unescorted. Planned: sign-in sheet at the stockroom door, escort rule, sheets kept 1 year, from 2026-10.
This SSP, approved 2026-08-31. It also documents the CMMC Level 1 assessment scope.
Workforce use rules are in POL-02 Part C (approved 2026-08-31). Gap: signed acknowledgments not yet collected.

baseline: Not in Moderate baseline (selected by tailoring)
implementation_statement: The Owner designated the Operations Manager as security and compliance lead in writing on 2026-07-06 and is the CMMC Affirming Official. Selected by tailoring (not in the Moderate baseline) because a named lead is needed at this size.

Gap: no termination checklist; access removal depends on memory (the former technician's ERP account). Planned: last-day checklist covering ERP, suite, supplier portals, carrier account, alarm code, keys, and MFA devices, by 2026-09-30.
Risk assessment completed 2026-07-24 using NIST SP 800-30 Rev. 1 with supply chain threats from SP 800-161 Rev. 1 (P01); the company's first. POL-02 requires an annual update.
Gap: no vulnerability scanning. Planned: quarterly external scan and monthly device scan by the MSP from 2026-12.

Contracts exist with the ERP vendor, suite vendor, and MSP (which resells the backup service). The ERP vendor's SOC 2 report was reviewed (P09). Gaps: no security review of the MSP; no written FCI safeguarding terms with the SaaS vendors that hold FCI; the ERP's AI subprocessor terms were never reviewed (P10).

The MSP-managed firewall blocks unsolicited inbound traffic and separates guest Wi-Fi. Gaps: the setup bench, which connects customer devices during configuration, and the cameras share the staff network; firewall firmware was last updated in 2024.
All SaaS traffic, including the customer portal, uses TLS provided by the vendors.
evidence: Vendor documentation; ERP vendor SOC 2 report

provider_if_inherited: ERP vendor; productivity suite vendor; MSP
implementation_statement: SaaS vendors encrypt stored data. The MSP encrypts the 8 laptops. Gap: the setup bench desktop, which holds customer settings files and equipment lists, is not encrypted.
The MSP patches the 9 computers monthly; SaaS vendors patch their platforms. Gaps: firewall firmware last updated in 2024; the camera recorder was never updated; no time limit for critical updates.

MSP-managed endpoint protection runs on all 9 computers with automatic updates, real-time scanning of files as they are downloaded or opened, and a weekly full scan. Alerts reach the MSP in business hours only (tracked under SI-4).

Gap: no monitoring beyond endpoint protection alerts. Planned: MSP-managed endpoint detection and response with after-hours alerting, and suite alerts for new forwarding rules and mass downloads, by 2026-12-31.

Gap: no supply chain risk management (C-SCRM) plan. Planned: a short plan based on NIST SP 800-161 Rev. 1 covering the sourcing order, broker approval, receiving inspection, Section 889 screening, and supplier notice terms, by 2026-11-30.
Supplier list kept by the buyer. Gap: the company's purchase orders to suppliers carry no flowdown of FAR 52.204-25 or DFARS 252.246-7008 and no supplier notice terms.

About 93% of purchase spend goes to authorized sources. Gaps: brokers are used whenever they are cheaper or faster, with no approval; no Section 889 screening list; 310 SKUs have no manufacturer of record.
evidence: Supplier list; ERP item master extract 2026-07-17

implementation_statement: Gap: no supplier assessments; the 4 brokers were never assessed for counterfeit prevention. Planned: one-page broker assessment and approval before any purchase, by 2026-11-30.
Gap: no supplier agreement requires notice of counterfeit, suspect, tampered, or covered items, or of a compromise affecting the company's orders. Planned: purchase order terms by 2026-10-31.

Gap: no inspection for tampering at receiving or at the setup bench. Planned: receiving checklist (seals, labels, weight, OEM serial validation for broker items) and a firmware version check at the bench, by 2026-10-31.

The ERP records serial numbers for every unit received and shipped, which supports tracing within the company. Gaps: no anti-counterfeit procedure, no traceability back to the original manufacturer for broker items, and no rule for reporting suspect items.
